limits: OBSERVED numbers on the shared reference machine; not portable guarantees. The host ran other MVP-0b agents concurrently (see load_start/load_end and per-category load_end).

cold/incremental `ms` measure the rustc process only (source files already written); daemon `ms` is end-to-end `Daemon::analyze` including hashing, snapshot sync and cache lookup, while daemon `timings.analysis_ms` isolates the compiler process.
the daemon does not do codegen, linking, artifact verification or activation: this is an analysis-stage measurement only
10 samples per cell: p95 is the 10th value, a coarse tail estimate, not a p95 confidence interval
the fixture is a small real library unit (~280 lines, 4 modules); absolute numbers scale with unit size and are not extrapolated to large crates

the daemon's stable compile-unit directory mirrors an editor that keeps the same file paths; snapshots are immutable but compilation happens from the stable unit, which is what makes -C incremental reusable. Compiling from a fresh directory per edit would invalidate the incremental cache.

measurement.cold_ms: wall time of one `rustc --emit=metadata --error-format=json` process, source files already written, fresh --out-dir per call, no -C incremental: the MVP-0a behaviour
measurement.correctness: diagnostic signature sets (severity, code, logical file, line, column, end_line, message) must be identical across all three modes for the same state; any mismatch fails the campaign
measurement.daemon_analysis_ms: daemon-internal `timings.analysis_ms`: rustc process wall time only, 0 on a cache hit
measurement.daemon_ms: end-to-end `Daemon::analyze` call (contract validation + SHA-256 identity + snapshot/checkout sync + cache lookup + compiler when needed), measured by the harness with Instant around the call
measurement.excluded: no codegen, no link, no artifact verification: this campaign measures the analysis stage only
measurement.incremental_ms: wall time of the same `rustc` invocation with a persistent `-C incremental=<dir>` across samples, source files already synced, same paths and same --out-dir
measurement.load: CPU busy ratio sampled over 250 ms, free physical memory, process count and `rustc -vV` spawn calibration are recorded at the start/end of every category
measurement.order: modes rotated per sample (cold/incremental/daemon, then incremental/daemon/cold, ...) to spread host-load drift across modes
measurement.percentiles: nearest-rank (ceil(p/100*n)-1), no interpolation; with 10 samples p95 is the 10th value
measurement.samples: 10 recorded samples per category and mode after one unrecorded warm-up call per mode

parallelism.note: campaign runs one compiler at a time; the daemon under test is configured with max_concurrent_jobs=1 (reference machine: 16 Go RAM, ~2 Go free)

rustc_reference_commands.daemon: ravum-daemon API: Daemon::analyze(AnalysisRequest) with -C incremental=<work>/incremental/<context> and content cache
rustc_reference_commands.incremental: same command with -C incremental=<persistent dir>, source files kept at the same paths
